chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad from Sahl from Ahmad ibn Abd al-Aziz who said, 'One of our companions narrated to me.'

Abu al-Hasan al-Awwal (peace be upon him), when he raised his head from the last rak'ah of Witr, would say: 'This is the station of one whose good deeds are a bounty from You, and his gratitude is weak, and his sin is great, and he has nothing except Your repelling [punishment] and Your mercy.'
For You said in Your Book Revealed upon Your Dispatched Prophet (peace be upon him): 'They used to sleep but little in the night, and in the morning they sought Forgiveness.'

My sleep has been long and my standing [in prayer] has been little, and this is the morning, and I am seeking Forgiveness from You for my sin, with the seeking of forgiveness of one who can find for himself neither harm nor benefit, nor death, nor life, nor resurrection.'
Then he would fall down in prostration (peace be upon him).

key_terms.الْأَسْحَارِ: The early morning hours before dawn
key_terms.رَكْعَةِ الْوَتْرِ: The last rak'ah of the Witr prayer

ai.seo_question: What is the supplication recited by the Imams after the Witr prayer?
ai.summary: Imam al-Hadi (peace be upon him) recites this profound supplication after the Witr prayer, highlighting the tension between human deficiency in gratitude and the magnitude of sin, thereby relying entirely on divine mercy. He explicitly quotes the Quranic description of the righteous who 'seldom sleep' and 'seek forgiveness at dawn' (51:17-18), connecting the Witr prayer's timing to the spiritual discipline of the *Sahar* (pre-dawn) hours. This practice underscores the Shia emphasis on *Tawakkul* (trust in God) and the efficacy of night worship as a means of expiation for those who feel their deeds are insufficient.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Muhammad, from Sahl, from Ahmad Bin Abdul Aziz who said, ‘One of our companions narrate to be saying,

‘It was so that whenever Abu Al-Hassanasws the 1st raised hisasws head from the last Rak’at of Al-Witr (Salāt), said: ‘This is a place of the one whose good deeds are a Bounty from Youazwj and his gratitude is weak, and his sins are great, and it is not for him except for Yourazwj Defence and Yourazwj Mercy,
for Youazwj Said in Yourazwj Book Revealed upon Yourazwj Dispatched Prophetsaww [51:17] They used to sleep but little in the night. [51:18] And in the morning they sought Forgiveness.

And little is my<sup>asws</sup> standing, and this is the morning and I<sup>asws</sup> am seeking Forgiveness from You<sup>azwj</sup> for sins of my<sup>asws</sup> (Shias) and seeking of the Forgiveness of the one who can neither find for himself a harm, nor a benefit, nor death, nor life, nor Resurrection’.
Then fall down in the Sajdah’.
en.sarwar: 16. Ali ibn Muhammad has narrated from Sahl from Ahmad ibn ‘Abd al-‘Aziz who has said that narrated to him certain persons of our people saying:

“When abu al-Hassan the first, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, raised his head from last sajdah of witr prayer he said, ‘This is a position of one whose good deeds are due to Your bounties and whose thanksgiving is weak, but his sin is great. He does not have anything other than Your defending him and granting him mercy.
You have said in Your book revealed to Your Holy Prophet and Messenger, “They sleep at night very little and in the morning ask forgiveness for their sins” (51: 18-19).

My sleep has been very long and my standing for Salah (prayer) very little. This is morning. I ask You to forgive me my sin, like the one who is unable to harm himself, or benefit, control his death, life or resurrection.’
Then he, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, would bow down to prostrate.”
